correctness.rationale: Every multiplier follows from the three-phase character filter, with explicit integer normalization. Dividing a hypothesized zero by its lowest power of -2 shows that its minimum exponent must appear exactly twice; the remaining exponent is one larger. Multinomial counting enumerates all zero frequency words, and Stirling yields the asymptotic loss density. A completely direct phase enumerator checked 29,520 Fourier frequencies and predicted ranks for n=2,...,9. The finite checks are corroboration, not a substitute for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Nowhere-zero finite-group flows on an n-parallel-edge dipole are a canonical support in enumerative graph theory and coding theory, but the full ambient Fourier inverse problem is a different natural invariant than their count. The theorem completely classifies which dimensions lose information, gives a precise multinomial number of invisible modes and a sharp first-order n^{-1} vanishing fraction along the singular progression. It is an all-parameter structural classification rather than a small numerical recomputation, and does not claim broad graph-generalization or new character orthogonality.
